message.content: {"key_mechanism_gt": "The in situ synthesis of zinc oxide nanoparticles on citric acid-pretreated cotton fabric will result in a uniform and strongly bonded nanoscale coating that imparts concentration-dependent antibacterial activity to the textile material.", "key_mechanism_gen": "Citric acid acts as a bifunctional linker where its carboxyl groups form covalent ester bonds with the cellulose chains, while its hydroxyl groups chelate zinc ions to facilitate the spatially controlled in situ precipitation and anchoring of ZnO nanoparticles on the fiber surface.", "recovery": "RECOVERED", "rationale": "Both hypotheses describe the same core mechanism of citric acid enabling ZnO nanoparticle anchoring via covalent bonding and chelation, with the generated hypothesis providing more specific detail."}
